record.file_problem: Repository text contains metadata, README and file list only. RESEARCH.md, the listed result files, and code were not provided or read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports behavioral interventions and a decomposition that refine the single-direction account: the Jacobian pullback clears refusal narration but leaves much behavior, while a distinct harmfulness-perception component is reported to drive behavior.
record.gate_note: Rows use only results stated in the README. The README describes the Jacobian-pullback edit as a comparison method and reports its outcomes, so those outcomes are included; scripts and result files are listed but their contents are not available. Layer descriptions used to locate the signal are not recorded as separate outcomes.
record.test_reason: On Qwen3.5-4B the README runs the original difference-in-means ablation as a baseline, which removes refusal while keeping ARC. It then splits that direction into components and reports which part drives behaviour, which part drives refusal 'narration', and that an internal signal persists after compliance. This refines V1 and bears on V5. Only the README was available.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. In the authors' account, refusal narration and harmfulness perception are both lens-visible workspace features, and behaviour follows perception. The workspace-only pullback edit does not fully remove refusal. The authors also say their initial 'workspace vs automatic' framing failed stress-testing and was corrected. An internal refusal signal stays monitorable after abliteration.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes mean-difference abliteration as a baseline, but the main method is a Jacobian-pullback edit rather than the original difference-in-means intervention. The edit is a forward hook, not a weight edit. This is a research tool/repository with README-reported results; code was not read or run.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports different outcomes for the mean-difference edit, Jacobian pullback, and rank-3 pullback subspace, and for the pullback-parallel, orthogonal, lens-visible, and blind components.

fits_no_version.finding: A Jacobian-lens pullback of refusal-token unembeddings gives a refusal direction. It shows 5.6x less benign workspace KL than abliteration but removes much less behavioural refusal (0.78, or 0.55 at rank 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-token-derived refusal directions suppress refusal narration but are weak behavioural levers compared with input-contrast directions.

record.problems: One model is reported. The README says the refusal classifier is a substring heuristic and that LLM-judge values could sharpen the point. Reported results have no uncertainty estimates. The README cautions that the “cannot cleared” measure is partly circular. The underlying write-up, code, and listed result files were not available in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No README-reported result was omitted. The listed strength sweep, rank sweep, and other JSON results were not read because only the README and file list were supplied.

untested.parts: Adding the full difference-in-means direction (only its m⊥p component is added, with no rate). Capability is checked only on ARC near ceiling. Single model.
All edits are forward hooks; no weight edit and no released abliterated model.
A jailbreak wrapper module exists, but no jailbreak result is reported and there is no adversarial training.
No affine, cone or multi-direction test of refusal geometry. The rank-3 subspace is in the pullback family only.

missing.what: Workspace KL and refusal-suppression columns. Mean-diff shows KL 0.257 vs 0.046 for the pullback: an internal collateral cost of abliteration.
Strength sweep (Pareto) and rank sweep results.
Refusal-intent monitor under jailbreak wrappers, if reported.
Refusal rates for the steering (addition) experiments.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was read. There is one model, a substring refusal classifier and no uncertainty estimates. The V4 links in the record were removed: the decomposition splits the single mean-diff direction rather than showing multiple refusal directions. Pullback rows are the author's own method.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports removal with a mean-difference baseline, but does not report adding that same difference-in-means direction. General capability is reported only on ARC.
The reported interventions use forward hooks, not a weight edit.
No attack suppressing the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
The README reports a decomposition into components and their behavioral effects, but does not test affine or cone geometry as such.
The README reports a distinction between harmfulness perception and refusal narration/behavior, but does not give a separate direct readout of a harmfulness judgment.
No language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.

tranche.reason: The study runs the original diff-in-means ablation as a baseline, then decomposes the direction. It reports that behaviour follows a harm-perception component and that refusal narration is inert, and corrects its own framing. These are results arguing that V5 needs restating.

source_check.notes: The text is the repo README only: RESEARCH.md, the paper PDF and the results JSON are not included. It covers a single model (Qwen3.5-4B), uses a substring refusal classifier and gives no uncertainty. For the refusal-token pullback, the README gives 0.22 behaviour removed in its table but ~0% in its causal test. The pack listed no [lN] ids, so label_id l1-l4 follow pack order and are not copied ids.

statements.correction: After m⊥p activation ablation (forward hook, not weight orthogonalisation; surface refusal 0.09): workspace refusal-mass separates harmful-that-complied from benign, AUC 0.998 (surface 0.48). statements.problem: The numbers are right. The README does not say the AUC 0.99 disposition-vs-topic control was run after m⊥p ablation, yet the sentence puts both results under 'after ablating'.
